## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 3/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
Survey what is actually working, right now, to attract interested learners to sign up for email mailing lists / newsletters, and diagnose why some approaches succeed while others fail.

CONTEXT ABOUT THE REQUESTER (for the niche-transfer filter, not the main scope):
- Mark runs Agile Pain Relief, a solo/small B2B consultancy teaching Scrum, Kanban, and Agile methods, now pivoting toward helping knowledge workers thrive with Generative AI.
- Audience = working professionals (Scrum Masters, product people, engineering leaders, knowledge workers).
- His current list-building tactics are NOT working: (a) a downloadable lead magnet, and (b) a quiz on Generative AI failure modes. Part of the value here is understanding WHY these two specific approaches may be underperforming.

SCOPE = "broad + niche filter": Survey what's working across creators, newsletter operators, course-sellers, coaches, consultants, and professional educators generally. Then explicitly flag which tactics transfer to a solo B2B expert selling training/thought leadership in the Agile + GenAI space, and why.

EVIDENCE BAR (report must include a mix of all four):
1. Named examples + numbers: specific people/companies with conversion rates, list-growth figures, or before/after data, cited to a source.
2. Practitioner case studies: detailed write-ups of what someone tried and why it worked or failed.
3. Benchmark / industry data: aggregate opt-in rates by lead-magnet type, channel, quiz vs ebook vs newsletter, average landing-page conversion rates, etc.
4. Mechanism explanations: the behavioral/psychological "why it works" behind each tactic.

CHANNELS = no preference: cover all major acquisition surfaces (website/blog on-site opt-ins, content upgrades, exit intent, quizzes; LinkedIn and other social; YouTube/video; podcasts; SEO; paid; referral/viral; partnerships/newsletter cross-promotion/recommendations like beehiiv/Substack) and let the evidence show where the leverage is.

SPECIFIC QUESTIONS THE REPORT SHOULD ANSWER:
- What lead-magnet / opt-in formats convert best today, and what are typical opt-in conversion rates by format (ebook/PDF vs quiz vs mini-course vs template/toolkit vs free email course vs live event/webinar vs community)? Cite benchmark data.
- Why do generic downloadable PDFs and quizzes often underperform now? What makes a quiz work vs fail specifically?
- What is working best for B2B / professional-services / expert-led audiences specifically (vs consumer creators)?
- Evidence on newsletter-first / "the newsletter IS the product" growth (Substack/beehiiv/ConvertKit era), recommendation networks, and cross-promotion.
- The role of the offer/promise and positioning vs the format: does specificity of promise beat format choice?
- Concrete before/after examples where someone changed their opt-in and measurably improved sign-ups.
- 3-5 concrete, prioritized recommendations for what Mark specifically should test next, grounded in the evidence.

Prioritize recent evidence (roughly 2022-2026) since tactics have shifted with AI and platform changes. Cite every claim.

## Claim under review
"Across 41,000+ opt-in forms analyzed, the overall average conversion rate is 22.16%, with 'learning resources' (webinars/courses) at 27.4% and interactive tools (calculators/quizzes) at 26.44%, both above the ebook/report format at 24.61%."

**Source:** https://www.mailerlite.com/blog/best-lead-magnet-statistics (secondary)
**Supporting quote:** "Learning resources (webinars, courses): 27.4% ... Interactive tools (calculators, quizzes): 26.44% ... Reports/ebooks: 24.61% ... Overall average: 22.16%"

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

# Lead Magnet Conversion Rate Analysis

## Conversion Rates by Type

**Overall Average:** "22.16%"

**Learning Resources:** "27.4%" (webinars, micro-courses, tutorials)

**Interactive Tools:** "26.44%" (quizzes, calculators, AI generators)

**Reports/Ebooks:** "24.61%"

## Data Source and Sample

The analysis examined "over 41,000 forms and pop-ups created by more than 10,000 paid MailerLite users" with at least 100 conversions per form.

**Publication Date:** March 13, 2026

**Author:** Duncan Elder

The dataset excluded low-volume forms, focusing only on accounts demonstrating sufficient engagement to provide statistically meaningful insights.

Analysis Of 41,000+ Forms - MailerLite","url":"https://www.mailerlite.com/blog/best-lead-magnet-statistics"},{"title":"TOP 20 LEAD MAGNET CONVERSION STATISTICS 2026 REVEAL THE SHOCKING OPT-IN REALITY","url":"https://www.amraandelma.com/lead-magnet-conversion-statistics/"},{"title":"Lead Magnet Conversion Benchmarks 2026 - Subpage.co","url":"https://subpage.co/lead-magnet-conversion-benchmarks-2026/"},{"title":"Lead Magnet Conversion Rate by Industry: 2025 - Focus Digital","url":"https://focus-digital.co/lead-magnet-conversion-rate-by-industry/"},{"title":"Lead Magnet Conversion Rate Calculator","url":"https://www.spreadsheetables.com/leadmagnetcalculator"},{"title":"Lead Magnet Statistics 2025 - 70 Mind-Blowing Figures","url":"https://mycodelesswebsite.com/lead-magnet-statistics/"},{"title":"Lead Magnet Conversion Rates - What You Need To Know • Magnnetic","url":"https://magnnetic.com/lead-magnet-conversion-rate/"},{"title":"67+ Lead Generation Statistics & Trends (2026)","url":"https://www.emailvendorselection.com/lead-generation-statistics/"}]

The 22.16% figure comes from a MailerLite study analyzing over 41,000 forms. Here's what the research reveals:

## The 22.16% Benchmark

The average conversion rate across all forms and pop-ups was 22.16%. This figure came from an analysis of signup forms and pop-ups created by more than 10,000 paid MailerLite users who had at least 100 conversions from their forms.

## Which Lead Magnets Beat the Average

Several categories outperformed this benchmark. The lead magnet categories for interactive tools, reports and ebooks, and checklists also performed well, with an average conversion rate of 26.44%, 24.61% and 23.22%, respectively. This is above the average of 22.16%.

Interactive tools led the way, and interactive tools include lead magnets like calculators, quizzes, and AI generators.

Consultation offers also performed strongly. Consultation and service lead magnets, which included offers such as calls, audits, strategy sessions, and demos, were the 5th-best-performing offer, with an above average conversion rate of 23.31%.

## Which Lead Magnets Fell Below the Average

Some notable underperformers included:

- **Templates:** The researchers found it surprising that templates had a slightly below-average conversion rate of 21.14%.

- **Discounts:** These had the worst performance. Forms and pop-ups offering a discount had the lowest conversion rate of any offer, at just 16.2%. The likely reason: discounts likely underperform because they're used as a blanket offer that gets shown to every website visitor. Offers that aren't targeted will always have a lower conversion rate than targeted ones.

## Additional Context

It's worth noting that this 22.16% average reflects on-site forms and pop-ups, and conversion benchmarks can vary widely by traffic source and format. For example, other 2026 benchmark data shows email traffic converts at 19.3%, paid search at 11.3%, organic search at 6.4%, and paid social at 3.1%. So context matters a great deal when comparing your own results against this figure.

content.text:
The claim checks out against its primary source. Let me record the verification.

The MailerLite blog (published March 13, 2026, author Duncan Elder) reports exactly the figures cited: overall average 22.16%, learning resources 27.4%, interactive tools 26.44%, reports/ebooks 24.61%, from an analysis of 41,000+ forms/pop-ups by 10,000+ paid MailerLite users with 100+ conversions each. Every number in the claim matches the source verbatim, and the framing (learning resources and interactive tools both above ebooks) is accurate.

Caveats that qualify but do not refute: (1) it is vendor first-party data with selection bias — only paid MailerLite users, only forms with 100+ conversions, so survivorship/engagement bias inflates the baseline; (2) these are on-site form/pop-up view-to-conversion rates on already-engaged visitors, a very different denominator than cold landing-page or channel benchmarks (the same page notes email traffic ~19.3%, organic search ~6.4%, paid social ~3.1%), so the 22% "average" should not be read as a universal opt-in rate; (3) the inter-format gaps are modest (27.4 vs 26.44 vs 24.61). None of these contradict the claim as written — the claim accurately reproduces and attributes the figures and does not overstate them.
